title: Ads, sales pages, broadcasts and emails that sell

say: Ads, sales pages, broadcasts and emails that sell.

say: PAS stands for Problem, Agitate, Solution. For example, Uche services generators in Owerri. Problem: does your generator start, run for a few minutes, then go off?

panel.heading: PAS: Uche's generator ad
items: Action: one tap, one next step

say: Agitate: you keep pulling the rope, food in the freezer starts to spoil, and you buy fuel for a machine that will not stay on. Factual, not frightening.

panel.heading: PAS: Uche's generator ad
items: Action: one tap, one next step

say: Solution: home servicing in Owerri, carburettor cleaning, plug and oil change, and a test run, from about 10,000 naira depending on size.

panel.heading: PAS: Uche's generator ad
items: Action: one tap, one next step

say: Action: tap Send WhatsApp message and tell us your generator brand and size.

panel.heading: PAS: Uche's generator ad
items: Action: one tap, one next step

say: Meta's ad standards do not allow copy that asks about someone's health, money or body. Are you broke? will be rejected. Does your generator keep going off? is about the generator, not the person.

panel.heading: PAS: Uche's generator ad
items: Action: one tap, one next step
panel.rule: Talk about the situation, not the person.

say: For example, Funke runs baking classes in Lagos. Her headline: Bake soft bread and cakes you can sell, in 4 Saturdays.

panel.heading: Follow the reader's questions
items: Headline: the promise, and who it is for

say: The problem: you have watched many videos, but your cakes still sink, and you are not sure how to price what you bake.

panel.heading: Follow the reader's questions
items: Headline: the promise, and who it is for

say: Benefits with proof: bake with your own hands, take home recipes, and learn to cost a recipe. Plus real student comments, shared with permission.

panel.heading: Follow the reader's questions
items: Headline: the promise, and who it is for

say: The offer: a fee of 60,000 naira, ingredients included. Only 12 seats per class, so everyone gets hands-on time. That limit is true, so the urgency is honest.

panel.heading: Follow the reader's questions
items: Headline: the promise, and who it is for

say: Then the FAQ, taken straight from her chats: do I need an oven at home? Can I pay in two parts? Answer honestly, never dodge. Then one button: Reserve my seat.

panel.heading: Follow the reader's questions
items: Headline: the promise, and who it is for

say: Words like amazing and expert tell the buyer nothing.

panel.heading: One detail beats three adjectives
right: Learn to cost a recipe for profit

say: Start each bullet with the result, and add one specific detail. Bake 6 recipes yourself, from bread to meat pie. And only write 8 years of experience if it is true.
Design for phones first: short paragraphs, small photos, and a button a thumb can reach.

say: A broadcast list sends one message privately to many contacts, but only people who saved your number receive it.
For example, Ifeoma sells fabric in Aba. She used to add every customer without asking, and shout in capital letters. Some blocked her.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's restock broadcast
left: All kinds of lace, very cheap
right: Good morning. Wine lace is back

say: Now she asks first: would you like new arrivals once a week? Reply YES to join, and STOP any time.
Her message is calm and specific: the wine Swiss lace is back, 5 yards for about 38,000 naira, 14 pieces with 6 reserved. Reply WINE to reserve one.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's restock broadcast
left: All kinds of lace, very cheap
right: Good morning. Wine lace is back

say: Ask permission first. It keeps people from blocking you, and respects Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023.

cards.d: Ask before adding anyone, and make leaving easy. It respects the Data Protection Act 2023.
One to two broadcasts a week often works better than daily. Mix offers with useful tips.
Tell your list your account number, and that you never ask for card PINs or OTPs.

say: Send one to two broadcasts a week, at a time customers are free, and mix offers with useful tips. If replies drop, you are sending too often.

cards.d: Ask before adding anyone, and make leaving easy. It respects the Data Protection Act 2023.
One to two broadcasts a week often works better than daily. Mix offers with useful tips.
Tell your list your account number, and that you never ask for card PINs or OTPs.

say: Scammers sometimes copy a seller's name and photo. Tell your list which account number you use, that you never ask for card PINs or OTPs, and send payment details only after a customer confirms an order.

say: For example, Ruth launches office lunches in Abuja. Not Ruth's Kitchen Update, but: Hot office lunches for your team, delivered by 12:30. She writes the preview text, offers one goal, a free tasting day, and adds a P.S. with an honest limit.
Only email people who agreed, never buy lists, and always include an unsubscribe link.

panel.heading: Before you send an email
items: Preview text written, not left blank
One goal, one button, a P.S.
Only people who agreed; unsubscribe link

say: To remember. Use PAS for felt problems and AIDA for desire. Describe situations, not people. Build sales pages in the order of the reader's questions. Ask permission before broadcasting. And give every email one goal.

panel.heading: Remember
items: PAS for felt problems, AIDA for desire
Sales page follows the reader's questions
Broadcasts: permission, one point, one action
